notes.title: Korean summers
notes.text: Seoul summers are hot and humid, with a rainy season (장마) in July. Fans, iced drinks, cold noodles (냉면) and patbingsu (shaved ice) are how people survive.

notes.title: Wearing verbs
notes.text: Korean has different "wear" verbs: 입다 for clothes, 신다 for shoes and socks, 쓰다 for hats and glasses, 끼다 for rings and gloves, 하다 for accessories like ties and scarves.

notes.title: Colors as adjectives
notes.text: Korean colors are often adjectives: 빨갛다 (to be red) → 빨간 셔츠 (a red shirt), 파랗다 → 파란 하늘 (a blue sky). Add 색 to make a noun: 빨간색 (red), 파란색 (blue).

notes.title: Moving-in gifts
notes.text: When you move into a new place in Korea, it's a nice custom to greet the neighbors (이웃) with a small gift — traditionally rice cakes (이사 떡), today often toilet paper or detergent, which "wish you good fortune that keeps unrolling."
